subject: Clarify DPA breach timelines, subprocessor evidence access & EU transfer expectations
messages:
From: Eliza Moreno <eliza@finserve.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: legal@datatrust.co
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Possible data exposure — DPA timelines and subprocessor evidence access

Hi Aisha,

We detected suspicious activity affecting a subset of production requests routed to our integration with Redwood last night. Our security team has flagged it as a potential data exposure and asked me to confirm the contractual obligations under the DPA, specifically:

- What initial acknowledgement timeline can Redwood commit to for EU customers? The DPA we signed references "prompt" notice but our regulator expects a 48-hour first-response window for preliminary status.
- What level of evidence/export can you provide (forensic snapshot, request logs, sample payloads)? Is there a standard export format and transfer mechanism?
- If a Redwood subprocessor holds relevant telemetry, what is the expected cooperation cadence and the cut you need from us to trigger subprocessor access or escrow?

We want to get aligned quickly — can you outline what information you need from us to start an evidence handoff and whether any contractual amendments are required for cross-border transfer to our EU controllers?

Thanks,
Eliza
Eliza Moreno
CTO, FinServe
From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Eliza Moreno <eliza@finserve.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — DPA timelines and subprocessor evidence access

Hi Eliza — thanks for the heads up and sorry you're dealing with this. We take these reports seriously. High level answers below; legal will weigh in on the contractual specifics.

1) Acknowledgement window: we can provide a preliminary acknowledgement within 24 hours of a verified report coming in to security@redwood.com. For EU-regulated customers we typically escalate internally to a 48-hour investigation cadence (prelim findings). I will confirm escalation path with Ben.

2) Evidence we can provide: our standard package is a redacted forensic snapshot (Kafka index + request metadata), a token-level request-log CSV (pseudonymized), and a system health snapshot (node-level metrics). We transfer via encrypted S3/HTTPS with short-lived credentials or SFTP on request. We do not send full unredacted payloads without a narrow legal basis.

3) Subprocessor cooperation: Redwood will coordinate access requests to the subprocessor but needs a written SOC/evidence request routed through our security/legal teams with a clear scope (time range, customer-identifiers, artifacts). If subprocessor access requires additional contractual steps (e.g., subproc SOP, export licenses) we'll flag it.

Action items: Ben / Kimberly — can you confirm whether we can commit to (a) 48-hour preliminary update for EU controllers and (b) the redacted snapshot template below? I'll propose a 30-minute sync with FinServe security for tomorrow.

Attached: DPA_ExhibitB_v3.pdf (excerpt of notification obligations), evidence_transfer_checklist.xlsx (operations draft).

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Possible data exposure — DPA timelines and subprocessor evidence access

Aisha / team — quick legal/ops guidance.

- Contractual stance: Exhibit B language in the DPA obligates "prompt" notice and cooperation. For regulated EU customers we have operationally accepted a 48-hour preliminary acknowledgement, followed by a 72-hour substantive update window when feasible. We should prefer 48h ack + 72h technical update (i.e., preliminary findings + containment steps).

- Evidence scope: We can provide the redacted snapshot (hashes, timestamps, routing metadata), request-identifier lists, and any replayable telemetry that does not include full PII or customer payloads. If FinServe requires full payloads, we need either a lawful basis memo or a narrowly-scoped Data Processing Amendment (DPA addendum) signed.

- Subprocessor engagement: Redwood will act as the coordinator. If the subprocessor is a third party bound under our standard subproc agreements (SOC2 + DPA flow-down), we can request an expedited evidence pull, but the subprocessor may require a subpoena or formal evidence request for payload-level exports.

- Cross-border transfers: for EU-origin data, transfers to non-EEA locations require SCCs (Standard Contractual Clauses) or equivalent safeguards. If the export is to a forensics provider outside EEA, ops/legal must document the transfer basis and log it.

Recommended reply to FinServe: confirm 24h ack / 48h EU preliminary update + 72h technical update cadence; offer the redacted snapshot and S3 transfer; state that full payload exports require a signed addendum or lawful basis. Also propose a short call to align scope and sign an access attestation.

I can draft a one-page addendum template (limited-scope forensic access) if they need payload-level exports.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security — Redwood Inference
From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Eliza Moreno <eliza@finserve.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — DPA breach timelines, subprocessor evidence access & EU transfer expectations

Eliza — short update and next steps after legal review:

- Acknowledgement: Redwood will send a formal acknowledgement within 24 hours of this thread. For EU controllers we will follow with a preliminary update within 48 hours and a technical update target of 72 hours where we can (we will surface any blockers).
- Evidence transfer: we can provide a redacted forensic snapshot and request-log CSV via encrypted S3. If you need payload-level exports we will prepare an addendum to the DPA (Ben will draft) and request a signed attestation from FinServe identifying lawful basis.
- Subprocessor: please confirm the specific subprocessor(s) you believe hold relevant telemetry. If access to a subprocessor is necessary, Redwood will coordinate and may request a minimal intake form (who, what, why, retention duration).

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync today 17:00 CET / 08:00 PT to confirm the time ranges and export delivery method?

Thanks — we'll keep this thread as the primary record.
